tasks.spec: A telemetry collector stores variable-size records in a bounded byte ring. Readers consume monotonically numbered records. Wrapping a record cannot overwrite unread bytes; oversized records are rejected. There is one writer and one reader, both represented by explicit methods rather than real threads.
tasks.question: Write a complete Python implementation, explain its invariants and wraparound representation, and provide tests covering empty/full states, variable record sizes, rejection, and repeated wraparound. Explain every ownership transition.

tasks.spec: A job broker orders runnable work by deadline and stable insertion order. Jobs can be rescheduled or cancelled after insertion. The heap may contain stale versions, but clients must never execute an obsolete version. IDs are arbitrary strings and deadlines are integer clock ticks.
tasks.question: Implement the broker in Python using a heap plus version tracking. Explain complexity, stale-entry cleanup, deterministic ties and how to test cancellation, rescheduling and ID reuse. Include a detailed worked execution trace.

tasks.spec: A build planner receives named tasks and their dependencies. Tasks can be requested in any order. It must detect cycles with an explanatory path, emit a stable valid order for acyclic tasks, and invalidate dependents after an input changes. The graph is small enough to keep in memory.
tasks.question: Provide complete Python code for validation, stable planning and transitive invalidation. Explain the algorithms and invariants. Include tests for disconnected graphs, diamonds, self-cycles, longer cycles and incremental changes.

tasks.spec: A byte stream contains frames with a four-byte unsigned big-endian length followed by payload bytes. Reads may split headers or payloads and may contain several frames. Payloads can be empty; lengths over 65536 are invalid. End of stream with an incomplete frame is an error.
tasks.question: Implement an incremental Python frame parser with feed and finish methods. Explain buffering, failure recovery and memory bounds. Include exhaustive split-point tests, multiple frames, empty frames, oversized lengths and truncated streams.

tasks.spec: A content store builds a manifest mapping normalized relative file paths to byte size and SHA-256. Absolute paths and parent traversal are invalid. Comparing two manifests must classify additions, deletions and content changes. Ordering and serialization must be deterministic.
tasks.question: Write a Python implementation with path validation, deterministic serialization and manifest comparison. Explain filesystem race assumptions and how to test Unicode paths, empty files, content changes with equal size and unsafe paths.

tasks.spec: A worker may receive duplicate jobs with the same idempotency key. The durable record can be pending, running, completed or failed. Leases expire after 30 clock ticks. A completed result must be returned on retry; a stale lease owner must not overwrite a newer owner's result.
tasks.question: Implement the state machine in Python with an injected clock and an in-memory transactional store. Explain fencing tokens, retries and failure cases. Include detailed tests for duplicates, lease expiry, stale completion and successful result reuse.

tasks.spec: An order service commits database changes and an outgoing event in the same transaction. A publisher sends committed outbox entries to a broker with at-least-once delivery. Subscribers must handle duplicates and preserve ordering per order ID. Broker outages can last several hours.
tasks.question: Design the complete outbox and consumer protocol. Include schemas, state transitions, pseudocode, batching, retry backoff, ordering, retention, observability and a failure-injection test plan. Explain where exactly-once claims would be misleading.

tasks.spec: A warehouse has eight packing stations and three loading docks. Each order requires a packing phase and a loading phase with known durations. Urgent orders have deadlines. Stations and docks may fail temporarily, and in-progress work cannot be moved instantaneously.
tasks.question: Design a scheduler with explicit resource ownership, deadline handling and recovery. Explain admission, priority inversion, fairness, cancellation and rescheduling. Include pseudocode, a worked schedule and tests for failures and capacity exhaustion.

tasks.spec: A distributed service stores versioned customer documents. Old and new application instances run concurrently during deployment. Migration must be resumable and preserve writes. Documents carry a schema version and revision number; some fields are renamed and split into two fields.
tasks.question: Design a safe expand-migrate-contract rollout. Explain reads and writes during each phase, optimistic concurrency, backfills, rollback, monitoring and failure recovery. Include example schemas, pseudocode and adversarial tests.

tasks.spec: A service receives 72 jobs per second. A worker spends 40 milliseconds of CPU and 20 milliseconds waiting per job. There are six CPU cores, and jobs share a storage link capped at 120 jobs per second. Arrival bursts double the rate for 15 seconds every five minutes.
tasks.question: Derive sustainable throughput and explain the role of concurrency, CPU time and waiting. Calculate queue buildup during bursts under several worker counts, estimate drain times, state assumptions and propose a measurement plan. Show the arithmetic step by step.

tasks.spec: Storage plan A has 180 milliseconds setup and 3 milliseconds per object. Plan B has 650 milliseconds setup and 0.8 milliseconds per object. Both share a 900 MB/s channel; each object is 2 MB. Setup cannot overlap transfer within a plan.
tasks.question: Derive the break-even object count with and without the bandwidth limit. Calculate total times for 20, 100, 500 and 2000 objects. Explain batching, overlap assumptions, sensitivity to object size and a practical benchmark design.

tasks.spec: Three replicas independently fail during a one-hour interval with probability 0.02 each. A read needs one available replica; a write needs two. A shared network outage has probability 0.005 and makes every replica unreachable. Ignore repair within the interval.
tasks.question: Derive read and write availability under independence and then including the shared outage. Compare two and three replicas, explain correlated failures and conditional probability, and work through numerical examples and sensitivity analysis.

tasks.spec: An append-only log contains updates and tombstones keyed by strings. Every entry has a strictly increasing sequence number. Compaction keeps the latest entry per key within a closed segment while preserving the information needed by readers whose snapshots may be older than the compaction watermark.
tasks.question: Implement a Python compaction planner with a snapshot watermark. Explain safe tombstone removal, segment replacement, crash recovery and sequence-number invariants. Include a thorough worked example and tests for concurrent snapshots and repeated compaction.

tasks.spec: Clients upload large objects in independently retried chunks. A server must verify checksums, track missing chunks, finalize atomically and garbage-collect abandoned uploads. Clients may restart or send duplicate chunks; two clients may accidentally reuse an upload ID.
tasks.question: Design the protocol, metadata schema and state machine. Include ownership, authentication assumptions, idempotency, atomic finalization, cleanup, resource limits and a detailed failure-injection test plan with pseudocode.

tasks.spec: A processor incurs 9 milliseconds dispatch overhead per batch and 1.4 milliseconds per item. The buffer holds at most 80 items. Items arrive at 160 per second and require a mean latency below 100 milliseconds. Assume periodic dispatch and explain when this assumption breaks.
tasks.question: Derive throughput, utilization and mean waiting time as functions of batch size and interval. Evaluate several concrete choices, identify feasible operating points, and analyze bursts, deadline tails and measurement error with worked calculations.

tasks.spec: A package resolver chooses one version per package from a finite repository. Requirements are inclusive integer version ranges. Packages can have transitive dependencies and conflicts. The resolver should return a deterministic solution or an explanation of the unsatisfied constraints.
tasks.question: Implement a small backtracking resolver in Python with propagation and rollback. Explain termination, deterministic choice order, conflict reporting and complexity. Include tests for diamonds, conflicting ranges, cycles and backtracking to an older version.

tasks.spec: A metrics service ingests timestamped samples from intermittently connected devices. Samples may arrive late, out of order or duplicated. Dashboards query fixed windows and may accept provisional results. Storage and aggregation workers have independent capacity limits.
tasks.question: Design ingestion, deduplication, watermarking and aggregate correction. Explain bounded state, backpressure, retention, recovery and query semantics. Include schemas, state transitions, pseudocode and a worked late-arrival example.

tasks.spec: A storage system compares three replicas with an erasure code using six data and three parity fragments. Each object contains 24 MB. A rack offers 2 GB/s of usable bandwidth; reconstructing one missing erasure fragment reads six available fragments. Ignore CPU encoding cost initially.
tasks.question: Calculate storage overhead, normal write traffic and repair traffic for both schemes. Analyze repair time for one and many lost fragments under shared bandwidth, explain failure-domain assumptions, and extend the model to include encoding CPU cost and concurrent foreground traffic.
